newsitem.title: USA: Motorola splits Computer Group unit in two.
newsitem.headline: Motorola splits Computer Group unit in two.

text.p: Motorola Inc's Computer Group division (MCG) unveiled Monday a new organizational structure that divides the group into two major divisions -- Commercial Products and Technical Products.
Motorola said that, effective immediately, each division will have separate profit and loss responsibility for its engineering, sales, marketing, finance, human resources and quality teams.

"These new divisions within MCG will allow us to focus our product activities in markets where MCG continues to have proven leadership, specifically in the embedded and Mac-compatible systems markets," said Joe Guglielmi, MCG's general manager.

Embedded systems are specialized computer chips used to control a component of a larger electronic systems, such as an appliance, automobile or aircraft. Mac-compatilbe are computers based on the Apple Computer Inc Macintosh design.

The Commercial Products Division, to be headed by Dennis Schneider, vice president and general manager, will focus on the Mac-compatible market, portable products and AIX servers. AIX is International Business Machines Corp version of UNIX.
Schneider was most recently MCG vice president and director of worldwide marketing.

He said the division's mission is to become a billion dollar-plus, international computer systems company by the year 2001 or before. No comparable figure for the current revenues of the division was immediately available.
Wayne Sennett, a corporate vice president and general manager, will lead the Technical Products Division. He was formerly MCG's vice president of worldwide field operations.
He will head the development and marketing of computer board products and computer systems platform products to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in technical and embedded markets.
